title: Unit Event — Walk on and on — Episode6 I Hope They Understand

meta.Event Outline: In preparation for their next event, Vivid BAD SQUAD, Arata and the others set out to write different songs based on a single theme. Akito and An take on the duty of making the new track, but Toya wishes that he could contribute to lighten their load.

rows.Line: Street SEKAI
se_event_walk_2022_002

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line:
Now then...
I've finished watering this row, so that just leaves...

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line:
Oh, Toya, come on in.
Actually, that sounds a bit strange since we're outside.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Are you watering the flowers in these beds, Miku?

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line: Yes, since I want them to keep growing.

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line:
Oh, that's right.
Kohane also arrived just now.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Azusawa's here?

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line: Yes, we heard from her that Akito and An have finished making their demo.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, that's right. Akito said, “Starting tomorrow, we'll be practicing with the demo and laying down vocals.”

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line: I see. You must be very excited about that.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Yes, I am.
And I need to do my best to put on the best performance of their songs that I can.

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line:
*Nod*
Good luck.

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line:
Oh, that's it for here.
Thank you for the lovely chat, Toya.

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line:
Once more, come on in.
What would you like?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: A-Aoyagi!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh, Azusawa, what a coincidence.

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line:
Hello, Toya!
It's been quite a while.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I apologize for not being able to visit lately. I've been busy and...

rows.Speaker: MEIKO
rows.Line: That's perfectly fine. We're just glad to see that you're well. Would you like your usual coffee?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, please.

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line:
Oh, hey!
What if Toya helped too?

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: Wait, Rin, shush!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Help with what...?

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line: Huh? Because... I'm so sorry!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: What's going on here...?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Oh, um...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: But it would be really nice to have Aoyagi on board...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: So, we've been keeping it secret from the others that...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I've recently been working on my own track.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: But I was having so much trouble on my own that I'm having KAITO and Rin help me as I go...

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: And that's okay with us. Actually, we've mostly just been observing since you're such a hard worker.

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line: Yeah, he's right! We know that you've been trying super duper hard!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
I had no idea...
Still, Azusawa, what made you want to do this?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: You, An and Shinonome can all write your own music, right...? That means I'm the only one who doesn't know how.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
But that's not your fault...
You're still relatively new to all this.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I know, but I don't feel great about that...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I know I'm being a little selfish by wanting to make my own track. I get that I should be focusing on putting on a good performance right now...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Am I asking for too much...?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
No, I don't think so.
That's just how life is, right?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I see...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: (Azusawa was going through the same thing.)

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I don't see any problems with that...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Huh...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: What's wrong with doing what you want to do? If I were in your position, Azusawa, I would've made the same decision.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: So, what do you need me to do?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Oh, um...! It's not completely done yet, but I was hoping that you'd listen to what I have and tell me what you think.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I've been rewriting some of it and I think it might've turned out pretty well. At the same time, I may've possibly lost sight of what kind of song I originally wanted it to be.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, I see...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Then, I'd like to give what you made a listen.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Th-Thank you so much! I'll play it now...!
se_event_walk_2022_001

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: (Hm? This melody...)

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: How was it...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Well...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I'm also yet to create anything that I feel is satisfactory, so I don't think that I'm in a position to be criticizing...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But its quality leaves a lot to be desired. The beat seems a bit off, which is affecting its overall sound.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Its overall sound...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: If that happens, you're going to have a tough time achieving any sort of harmony, and what you originally imagined is going to fall apart.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I see. That explains why I didn't feel too confident about it. The more I worked on it, the further and further I got from what I initially wanted...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Songwriting's so hard...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But I don't think it's bad, since I believe that only you are capable of producing this song, Azusawa.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: By the way, did you use a part of one of Shiraishi's songs for the chorus?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Huh? Y-Yeah, you could tell...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, it sounded very much like the way Shiraishi puts together songs.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: You seemed to have listened very closely to what she made and tried whatever you could to make sure her sound didn't go to waste.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Overall, Azusawa, it's very like you.
I think it's a good expression of your honesty and tactfulness.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: It's easy to tell that you put quite a lot of thought into how things would sound moving into the chorus.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: There's this sort of excitement. This nervousness and joy centered around creating your own music for the first time.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line:
That's incredible, Aoyagi.
This song's supposed to be based on what I felt when I heard An sing for the first time.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Still, how did you figure all that out?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: How? Well...

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: Does your background in classical music have something to do with that?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Huh?

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line: Oh, you mean the way he broke down her song just now?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: The way he broke down my song?

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: Yes. Classical musicians place importance on playing a composer's music exactly the way they originally intended, no?

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: They'll research their background and what kind of person they were before attempting to play their work. That requires good analytical skills.

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: Based on what Toya did just now, I suspect he's very good at breaking down songs in such a manner.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh...

rows.Speaker: Toya's Father
rows.Line: No, again. Your rhythm is off. How many times do I have to tell you? This piece needs to be played slowly, while evoking strong emotions.

rows.Speaker: Toya's Father
rows.Line: You did it again. Why does this keep happening? You have a bad habit of rushing after you've realized what you've done. Can't you play it more gently?

rows.Speaker: Toya's Father
rows.Line: This is a practice piece that the composer was kind enough to write for our family. Happy was likely the last thing he felt as he wrote this... So, if you understand that, you should know how to play this song.

rows.Speaker: Toya's Father
rows.Line: Did you actually take a close look at the sheet music, Toya? You need to think more about what was going through the composer's mind. If you did, you would know how to play this piece already. You're done practicing. Go reread the sheet music again.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, my dad was very strict with me when it came to teaching me how to play classical music properly...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: In particular, he felt very strongly about understanding what was going on with the composer as they composed a song and reproduce that musically.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I also admired the way he could play... I don't know if I'm actually good at it, but I did my best to learn how to analyze sheet music.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I may've been able to understand Azusawa's song because she and I have been performing together for a while now.

rows.Speaker: Miku
rows.Line: That means you have the power to truly understand what a person's music is about, Toya.

rows.Speaker: KAITO
rows.Line: It goes perfectly with your kind personality.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Thank you, Aoyagi.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line:
The thing is...
When I decided that I was going to make my own track, I wanted you guys to feel something special when you listened to it...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: That's why I chose to turn the moment I met An for the first time into a song.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: My goal was to express the incredible joy and excitement I've felt every single day since she introduced me to the world of music.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: But I'm still not very good at songwriting, and really worried that my song isn't doing its job...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Which is why I was really happy when you said that you understood what feelings went into it, Aoyagi.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
I see...
Then, Azusawa, I'm glad I could figure out what you were feeling.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: It's nice to hear that everything I did back then is proving to be so useful now.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: So, thank you as well.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Huh? Y-You're welcome...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
(Still, Azusawa really impressed me.
She was clearly able to turn her feelings into a song.)

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: (I need to learn to do the same...)
